column3: Hebrew presents the building as completed; BSB uses present “builds.” The second subject is “folly.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew puts a rod of pride in the fool’s mouth; BSB adds its coming to his back.
Hebrew describes the manger as clean; BSB has “empty.”
Hebrew uses the image of breathing out lies; BSB says “pours forth.”
Hebrew presents the seeking as completed; BSB uses present “seeks.”
Hebrew names “lips of knowledge” and says they have not been known; BSB speaks of gaining knowledge from his speech.
Hebrew identifies folly as deceit; BSB makes folly actively deceive the fools.
Hebrew names guilt; BSB interprets it as the making of amends.
Hebrew expressly says “bitterness of its soul”; BSB has “its own bitterness.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew ends with plural “ways of death”; BSB has a singular way.
Hebrew states joy’s end as sorrow; BSB qualifies it with “may.”
Hebrew’s final phrase is “from what is with him”; BSB supplies a reward for his ways.
Hebrew has singular “his step”; BSB has plural steps.
Hebrew describes the fool’s anger and confidence; BSB has “careless and reckless.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew presents the inheriting as completed; BSB uses present “inherit.”
Hebrew presents the bowing as completed; BSB uses present “bow.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The second Hebrew clause names loving devotion and truth without an explicit verb “find.”
Hebrew expressly says “word of lips”; BSB has “mere talk.”
Hebrew repeats “folly”; BSB renders the first occurrence “effort.”
Hebrew says “souls” and uses the image of breathing out lies; BSB has “lives” and “utters.”
Hebrew begins with “in the fear of the LORD”; BSB makes a person who fears Him the subject.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew retains the contrasting images “long of anger” and “short of spirit”; BSB uses patient and quick-tempered.
Hebrew identifies envy as the bones’ decay; BSB turns decay into an active verb.
